title: Viz ICH Plus flags a brain hemorrhage and alerts a transfer team, and a 47-year-old man is transferred to a stroke center in 101 minutes
summary: Viz ICH Plus flagged a brain hemorrhage on a 47-year-old man's scan and alerted a transfer team, which moved him in 101 minutes against a 199.7-minute average.
account: A 47-year-old man came to the transferring hospital of the authors' large urban health system. He had severe headache, nausea and vomiting but no speech or motor deficits. The paper names neither the hospitals nor the city. All authors are at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York. An institutional review board had approved a study named ADVANCE, which was evaluating the software's accuracy and usability in the health system at the time. Viz ICH Plus (Viz.ai) analyzed his computed tomography (CT) scan and revealed a substantial right parieto-occipital hematoma with ventricular extension. It automatically alerted the Neuroemergencies Management and Transfer team at the receiving specialized stroke center. With an intracerebral hemorrhage score of 2, he was transferred within 101 minutes across 13.7 miles, against an average interhospital transfer time of 199.7 minutes. The 199.7-minute comparator comes from a 2021 series of 89 transferred patients in a New York City hospital system, whose authors include two authors of the case report. Those patients traveled an average of 13.6 kilometers. He had supratentorial craniotomy with endoscopic evacuation of the hematoma and placement of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt. His modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score was 4 and his National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 6 at one month. At three months the scores were 3 and 5. At one year they were mRS 1 and NIHSS 2. Follow-up CT scans at six and 12 months showed no recurrent hemorrhage or infarct.
purpose: Viz ICH Plus is built to detect intracranial hemorrhage on non-contrast CT and automatically notify care and transfer teams. Faster interhospital transfer is its intended function.
deployer: Large urban healthcare system, not named in the report; the city is not stated, and all authors are affiliated with Neurosurgery, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York
segment: AI hemorrhage detection with automated transfer notification

ratings.reason: After a hemorrhage with ventricular extension, the patient improved from a modified Rankin Scale score of 4 at one month to 1 at one year. The software's share is the time saved in transfer, and surgery was the treatment.
Interhospital transfer took 101 minutes against the system's 199.7-minute average, and the receiving team was engaged before the patient left the first hospital.

ai_role.statement: The software detected the hematoma and alerted the receiving transfer team, which advised on stabilization and arranged the transfer. A CT ordered for severe headache would have shown the bleed in any case, so the AI's contribution is the speed of notification and transfer. The authors write that, without it, care would have waited for a radiologist's read and a chain of calls. The comparison is one patient against a historical average with no matched control. The case report declares no financial relationships for any author, while Dr Kellner discloses research grant support from Viz.AI in a 2025 paper on the same software.

display.answer: The case rests on one case report by authors in the neurosurgery department of the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, published on 18 March 2025. Its 199.7-minute comparison comes from a 2021 series of 89 transferred patients whose authors include two authors of the case report.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Viz ICH Plus flagged a brain hemorrhage on a 47-year-old man's scan and alerted a transfer team, which moved him in 101 minutes against a 199.7-minute average.
fields.account: A 47-year-old man came to the transferring hospital of the authors' large urban health system. He had severe headache, nausea and vomiting but no speech or motor deficits. The paper names neither the hospitals nor the city. All authors are at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York. An institutional review board had approved a study named ADVANCE, which was evaluating the software's accuracy and usability in the health system at the time. Viz ICH Plus (Viz.ai) analyzed his computed tomography (CT) scan and revealed a substantial right parieto-occipital hematoma with ventricular extension. It automatically alerted the Neuroemergencies Management and Transfer team at the receiving specialized stroke center. With an intracerebral hemorrhage score of 2, he was transferred within 101 minutes across 13.7 miles, against an average interhospital transfer time of 199.7 minutes. The 199.7-minute comparator comes from a 2021 series of 89 transferred patients in a New York City hospital system, whose authors include two authors of the case report. Those patients traveled an average of 13.6 kilometers. He had supratentorial craniotomy with endoscopic evacuation of the hematoma and placement of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt. His modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score was 4 and his National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 6 at one month. At three months the scores were 3 and 5. At one year they were mRS 1 and NIHSS 2. Follow-up CT scans at six and 12 months showed no recurrent hemorrhage or infarct.
